steps.say: Nerve injuries grade like burns. First degree recovers in weeks, fifth needs a surgeon, and the bedside signs tell them apart.
steps.tx: **Seddon-Sunderland grades** (nerve injury scale) run **neurapraxia** (grade I, conduction block, full recovery) through **axonotmesis** (grades II to IV, grades 2 to 4, axon lost, Tinel advancing **1 mm per day**) to **neurotmesis** (grade V, transection needing repair), with EMG fibrillations confirming axon loss at three weeks.

steps.say: Time is muscle. Motor endplates die within eighteen months, so repairs happen early and gaps get grafts.
steps.tx: Nerve repair is done within days for clean cuts and before **6 months** (six months) for closed injuries, with **nerve graft** (bridge nerve piece) bridging gaps above **2 to 3 cm** (two to three centimetres), since **motor endplates** (muscle receivers) vanish after **12 to 18 denervated months** (one to one and half years) without hope.

steps.say: Night pain with clumsy thumbs means the median nerve is squeezed. Shaking the hand for relief is almost diagnostic.
steps.tx: **Carpal tunnel** (wrist nerve squeeze) gives night pain with **Phalen test** (bend test) and Tinel signs (tap tests) then **thenar wasting** (thumb muscle loss), confirmed on **nerve conduction** (electric speed test), and transverse carpal ligament release cures most cases durably, with thenar wasting marking late surgical disease.

vis.caption: Entrapment deformities: wrist drop, ulnar claw and thenar wasting. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Clawed fingers with a weak pinch localise the ulnar nerve, while birth patterns of arm palsy name the plexus level.
steps.tx: **Ulnar cubital compression** (elbow nerve squeeze) gives clawing with **Froment sign** (paper pinch bend), **Erb C5-C6** (upper trunk injury) gives waiter's tip, and **Klumpke C8-T1** (lower trunk injury) gives medial hand claw with **Horner syndrome** (droop triad) from T1 sympathetic injury.

steps.say: Forehead sparing separates brain from nerve. A smooth forehead with a drooping mouth is Bell palsy, not a stroke.
steps.tx: **Bell palsy** (face nerve failure) is a **lower motor neuron facial palsy** (whole side weakness) with **forehead involvement** (brow weakness) plus hyperacusis and taste loss, treated with steroids within **72 hours** (three days) plus eye care, with **70 percent full recovery** (seven in ten heal) by months.

vis.caption: Peripheral versus central facial palsy patterns. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Six spots plus freckles plus lumps equals NF1. Bilateral deafness tumours mean NF2 instead.
steps.tx: **NF1** (spot tumour illness) needs **6 or more cafe-au-lait spots** (coffee birthmarks) plus Lisch nodules, optic glioma or neurofibromas, while **NF2** (paired tumour illness) gives bilateral **vestibular schwannomas** (hearing lumps) with **merlin loss** (brake protein gone) and LZTR1 marks schwannomatosis.

vis.alt: Skin panels of smooth and irregular cafe-au-lait macules with axillary freckling.
vis.caption: Cafe-au-lait macules and axillary freckling in NF1. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Ash-leaf patches with baby spasms mean tuberous sclerosis. Vigabatrin stops the spasms while everolimus shrinks the brain lumps.
steps.tx: **Tuberous sclerosis** (potato skin illness) shows **angiofibromas** (face bumps), shagreen patches and cortical tubers with infantile spasms treated by **vigabatrin** (spasm drug), and **SEGA tumours** (ventricle lumps) shrink with **everolimus** (growth blocker) under drug levels, with renal angiomyolipomas watched alongside brain lesions.

steps.say: Port-wine foreheads seize while VHL families grow vessel tumours. Both need staged, gene-aware care.
steps.tx: **Sturge-Weber** (birthmark brain illness) gives V1 **port-wine stain** (red face mark) with **tram-track calcification** (rail lines) and leptomeningeal angioma causing seizures, and **VHL** (vessel tumour illness) combines haemangioblastoma with renal cancer and **phaeochromocytoma** (adrenal storm lump) needing staged resection, with retinal angiomas screened yearly in carriers.
